title: Coverage over repetition: spend the same 48k-step budget on ~48k fresh-rotated distinct vantages instead of 6000 static crops replayed 8x
hypothesis: The metric is limited by training coverage, not architecture. The baseline's 1993.71 m is ~29% of Berlin's map extent (regression-to-the-mean), and experiment 2's head reparameterization changed nothing (2136.91 m, reverted) — its own pre-registered refutation signature says the trunk's features can't separate locations. But train.py shows why: training samples 6000 of ~78,000 lattice positions (~8%) ONCE, freezes one rotation per crop, and replays those 6000 static images for 8 epochs (29 s total). The frozen v2 split guarantees every eval viewpoint is 11-17 m from a lattice framing, yet the 6000-crop subsample silently re-creates the v1 pathology inside the training procedure: the nearest actually-trained vantage averages ~44 m from an eval viewpoint (Poisson nearest-neighbor at 6000 points over 47 km^2), with a mismatched frozen heading, and 92% of vantages are never shown to a model whose entire premise is memorizing its box. A memorization model cannot memorize a map it was never shown. Streaming the full lattice with fresh per-visit rotations at the SAME step count isolates data coverage/freshness as the single variable: any gain is attributable to the data diet, not extra compute.
method: Rewrite model/train.py's data procedure only: replace load-once-static-tensor training (load_training_tensors -> one fixed 6000-crop tensor reused every epoch) with epoch-wise streaming over a global shuffled permutation of the FULL train lattice (~78k positions from pipeline.dataset.list_crops), consuming max_crops_per_bucket x n_buckets positions per epoch (6000/epoch at harness defaults, reshuffling when the permutation is exhausted), extracting each 128x128 crop on the fly per batch with a freshly drawn uniform(0,360) rotation at every visit. Architecture (model/model.py), loss, optimizer, batch size, and total gradient-step count are all unchanged — with harness defaults (EPOCHS=8, TRAIN_CROPS=6000) the model sees 48,000 presentations either way; this experiment changes only WHICH images those presentations are: ~48k distinct vantages (~62% of the lattice, mean eval-to-nearest-trained-vantage distance ~16 m) instead of 6000 vantages repeated 8x (~44 m).
expected_outcome: Worst-case median error (single 'asis' bucket on this branch) drops from 1993.71 m to the 800-1500 m range: breaking the 92%-never-seen data diet should loosen regression-to-the-mean even at fixed step count, though single-visit-per-vantage training and TinyLocNet's 128-d GAP descriptor may under-memorize relative to a multi-pass regime. Success = kept by the harness (clearly below 1993.71 m). Wall-time stays small (~2-5 min on MPS: identical step count plus ~150 us/crop extraction overhead); ONNX unchanged at ~0.4 MB (gate 4 MiB). Refutation signature: score stays ~2000 m at full coverage, which exonerates training-data scale at this compute level and makes trunk capacity / descriptor pooling the prime suspect — in that case the next experiments should scale compute (more total steps over the full lattice) or revisit exp 2's classification head under this fixed training regime.
eli5: This model is supposed to memorize what every part of Berlin looks like from above, like a taxi driver memorizing a city. But it turns out we were only ever showing it 8% of the flashcards — the same 6,000 photos over and over, always held at the same angle — and then quizzing it on the whole city. We didn't give it more study time; we made every flashcard in the same study session a new place, held at a new angle. Same effort, spent on seeing the whole city once instead of a small corner eight times.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only, no synthetic lighting variants

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: Small 4-layer conv stack that boils the image down to a 128-number fingerprint of what the ground looks like

stages.name: Coordinate regressor
stages.detail: Single linear layer maps the 128-number fingerprint straight to a position on the map

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: Self-check score in [0,1]; below 0.3 the fix is discarded as an abstention

stages.name: Position output
stages.detail: Regressed map position converted to (lat, lon, confidence)

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: Same training effort as before, but every practice image is now a different spot on the map seen from a freshly random angle, instead of the same 8% of spots repeated eight times

implementation_brief:
Edit model/train.py ONLY. model/model.py is UNTOUCHED (build_model, loss_fn, export_onnx, estimate_position all stay exactly as they are).

FIXED CONTRACTS (restated — the frozen harness depends on these):
- CLI must remain exactly: python -m model.train --area <a> --out-dir <d> [--data-dir <d>] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket N] [--seed N]. loop.sh invokes it as: python -m model.train --area berlin --out-dir $RUN_DIR/train_berlin --epochs 8 --max-crops-per-bucket 6000. All flags keep their names and defaults (epochs=2, max-crops-per-bucket=800, seed=0).
- ONNX export contract (model/model.py docstring): one ONNX per area at <out-dir>/models/<area>.onnx, input 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output [[u, v, conf]]. Unchanged because export_onnx and the model are unchanged.
- <out-dir>/train_info.json must still be written as a JSON LIST that is appended to if it exists, and the info dict must still be printed as the final JSON line. Keep existing keys: area, n_train_crops, epochs, device, train_seconds, onnx_bytes, init ('from-scratch').

CHANGES in model/train.py:
1. DELETE load_training_tensors. It preloads one fixed subsample into a single tensor — the mechanism this experiment removes.
2. In train_area, before the epoch loop: load meta; build crops = list_crops(area, meta['width'], meta['height'], 'train') (the FULL lattice — never subsample this list); load each bucket image once into a dict {bucket: np.asarray(Image.open(area_dir(area, data_dir) / 'relight' / f'{bucket}.png'))} (uint8, kept as-is in RAM; on this branch LIGHTING_BUCKETS has the single key 'asis', ~142 MB — do NOT convert whole images to float).
3. Streaming schedule: crops_per_epoch = min(max_crops_per_bucket * len(LIGHTING_BUCKETS), len(crops)) (= 6000 at harness defaults). Maintain a global shuffled permutation of range(len(crops)) drawn with the existing np.random.default_rng(seed) rng; consume the next crops_per_epoch indices each epoch, and reshuffle+restart the permutation when fewer than crops_per_epoch remain (so distinct vantages accumulate across epochs and nothing repeats until the whole lattice has been visited).
4. Per epoch, iterate that epoch's indices in minibatches of 64 (keep batch size 64 and Adam lr=1e-3 exactly as now). For EACH crop in the batch, AT VISIT TIME: pick a bucket (rng.integers over the bucket list — constant on this branch), draw a FRESH angle = float(rng.uniform(0, 360)), call extract_crop(img, c['cx'], c['cy'], angle), and target crop_center_norm(meta, c['cx'], c['cy']). Stack ONLY the minibatch into a float32 tensor (/255.0, NCHW) and move it to device. NEVER materialize more than one minibatch of float pixels at a time — the full lattice as float32 would be ~15 GB.
5. Keep per-epoch mean-loss print lines in the same format ('[area] epoch i/N loss=...'). Keep n_train_crops in train_info as the TOTAL number of presentations (epochs * crops_per_epoch, i.e. 48000 at defaults — comparable to the baseline's 6000*8 replay count is NOT what it recorded; baseline recorded 6000, so to stay honest add two NEW keys instead: 'distinct_train_vantages' (count of unique lattice indices actually visited) and 'presentations' (total crops shown), and set n_train_crops = presentations with a one-line comment noting the semantic change).
6. Seeding: keep torch.manual_seed(seed) and the single rng for permutation + angles + bucket picks so runs are reproducible.
7. Do not add multiprocessing/DataLoader workers (macOS + MPS spawn pitfalls; per-batch extraction is ~150 us/crop and fast enough). Do not change device selection, export, or the __main__/argparse block beyond what is described.

What stays untouched: model/model.py entirely; loss function and its 0.5 conf threshold; optimizer, lr, batch size, epoch count semantics (still 'epochs' outer loops); ONNX export call; train_info.json append/print behavior.
